messages:
maya: Heads up — noticed a 3x spike in preemptions in eu-west3 over the last 10m. Impacting some low-latency endpoints. Any ideas on quick mitigations?
liam: link to dashboard?
maya: https://grafana.internal/redwood/spot-health?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west3 — preemptions_total and eviction_rate panels.
infra-bot: ALERT: VM_POOL_PREEMPTION_RATE high (eu-west3) — 10m avg = 2.9% ; triggered at 1943215480.
liam: hmm our backfill policy currently tries to fill with cheapest spare capacity which is mostly preemptible. we should prioritize a small on-demand reserve for hot routes.
sophia: agree. suggest introducing priority buckets: hot (on-demand fallback), warm (mixed), cold (preemptible). Start by reserving ~5-10% of capacity for hot routes.
maya: can we implement a soft backfill switch first? prefer on-demand if eviction_rate > 1.5% for that zone.
devon: +1. we already have zone-level metrics. quick prometheus query:
```
sum(rate(preemptions_total{region="eu-west3"}[5m])) by (zone)
/ sum(machine_count{region="eu-west3"}) by (zone)
```
use that as an interruption_rate signal.
liam: and tie it to routing policy: if interruption_rate(zone) > 0.015 then mark zone as "avoid_for_hot" for 10m.
sophia: we should also avoid thrashing — add hysteresis: require 3 samples (5m each) before switching, and back off only after 30m stable.
maya: good. what's the quick alert change? current alert fires at 1% and floods the channel. can we create a composite alert that only fires if SLO impact > 0.2% and interruption_rate > 1.5%?
devon: propose composite metric:
```
composite_slo_impact = max(estimated_slo_loss, interruption_rate * weight)
```
Then alert when composite_slo_impact > 0.002.
liam: rough estimation is fine for now. estimated_slo_loss = (requests_routed_to_zone * avg_latency_penalty) / total_requests 
we can approximate with tail latency delta * pct_traffic.
sophia: I'll draft the alert rule and a short playbook. It will: 1) suppress noisy alerts, 2) call out zone & routes affected, 3) include suggested mitigation (flip hot routes to on-demand reserve or lower concurrency).
maya: mitigation steps for runbook:
- check preemptions graph (eu-west3)
- if interruption_rate > 1.5% and composite_slo_impact > 0.002 -> flip hot routes to on-demand bucket (5-10%)
- enable graceful degradation: lower max_tokens and increase timeout to preserve throughput on mixed pools
- trigger infra-bot notify and start 30m cooling timer
- after 30m, evaluate and either revert or extend fallback
liam: add cost note: reserving 5-10% on on-demand will increase cost ~+7-12% for that pool. but should be cheaper than repeated retries & degraded UX.
devon: can we test in staging? run a canary where we simulate 2.5% preemptions and measure effect of 5% reserve on tail latency.
sophia: yes — I'll spin up a staging mix of capacity and run the failure injection harness. plan: A/B 20% traffic for 1h.
maya: timeline?
sophia: will post the alert rule PR by EOD, runbook by tomorrow, and schedule canary for Thursday.
liam: thumbs up. after canary we should add a sensor that predicts preemption bursts using recent slope of preemptions_total — early warning often gives ~10-20m lead.
maya: thanks team. if anyone sees noise from the composite alert when I push changes, ping me directly. :pray:
